newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila's Napocor offers single-day power contracts.
newsitem.headline: Manila's Napocor offers single-day power contracts.

text.p: The Philippine's state-run National Power Corp (Napocor) is offering single-day power sales contracts to interested companies at a price lower than the prevailing rate.
Napocor president Guido Delgado said on Tuesday the contracts will hopefully convince customers owning power plants to shut down their facilities and instead buy power from Napocor.
"Our main objective is to maximize the use of our power plants. Running these small facilities will be more costly from the perspective of the whole Philippine economy," Delgado said in a statement.
Delgado said the power firm will present the new scheme to the Energy Regulatory Board (ERB) for approval.
Prior to the scheme, Napocor entered into sales pacts of longer periods and with rates higher or the same as the grid price.
About 220-megawatts of electricity are being generated daily by companies with their own power plants.

Many of them had set up their own power plants in the early nineties when the country was hit by a severe power crisis and many parts of the country used to be without power for several hours each day.
